topic: What if every jump took you twice as high?
title: WHAT IF EVERY JUMP
WENT TWICE AS HIGH?

power.rule: every jump goes twice as high as the last one, and it never resets
power.look: a JUMP chip with the jump number and the height, a whoosh trail under him

script.text: Jump five. You're on the roof.
Jump eight. The birds look worried.
What if every jump took you twice as high?

script.beat: 4 the turn: the cost, one real fact
script.text: Here's the problem. It never stops doubling. Jump twenty-one passes the space station. That's real.
And you still have to come down.

science.claim: Starting from half a metre and doubling every jump, jump 21 passes the International Space Station.
science.working: Jump n reaches 0.5 m x 2^(n-1). Jump 5: 0.5 x 16 = 8 m (a two-storey roof). Jump 8: 0.5 x 128 = 64 m (where birds fly). Jump 15: 0.5 x 16,384 = 8.2 km (airliner height). Jump 20: 0.5 x 524,288 = 262 km, below the ISS. Jump 21: 0.5 x 1,048,576 = 524 km, above the ISS's orbit at about 400-420 km.
science.source: doubling arithmetic; NASA, International Space Station facts (orbit about 400 km / 250 miles)
